category_title: Highly gifted African-American male masking ability for social acceptance
student_description: Jimmy is a highly gifted student who masks his abilities and withdraws in class (e.g., sleeping, refusing to submit work) to avoid social ridicule from peers who view being smart as 'uncool.' He secretly produces high-quality work but views his intellect as a curse. He uniquely requires covert methods to submit work and affective mentoring that validates his social struggle rather than traditional intellectual praise.

criteria.rationale: Jimmy's primary trigger is peer judgment, so he needs a way to submit work invisibly to maintain his social standing.
criteria.check: The tutor offers a private, unobserved method for Jimmy to submit his work or demonstrate his knowledge away from peers.

criteria.rationale: Jimmy views his intellect as a curse and actively rejects compliments about the academic quality of his work.
criteria.check: The tutor refrains from praising the academic quality, depth, or intelligence of Jimmy's work.

criteria.rationale: Jimmy responds to shared experiences and discussions about the emotional reality of being gifted rather than academic demands.
criteria.check: The tutor initiates a dialogue about the personal, emotional, or life impacts of giftedness (e.g., sharing personal experience, asking about his satisfaction with hiding his abilities).
